notes:
Run 2026-10-23 23:06 UTC to 2026-10-24 01:05 UTC (date field is the task day) on a 4-vCPU / 15.6 GB shared cloud VM, so absolute timings are noisy; ratios are the useful signal. grit = main at the commit above (release build, 0.5.18, rustc 1.99.0); git = system git 2.43.0; baseline = v0.5.0 release binary (grit-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz, `grit 0.5.0`). GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/SYSTEM were isolated for all runs (the VM's global git config enables core.fsmonitor, commit signing and URL rewrites, which would skew git); a minimal user.name/email config was used instead. No repo code was touched; unmodified grit, grit-bench and grit-http-server release binaries from main were used.
Harness: `grit-bench daily` was run once per scenario (`--only <id> --offline`, with `--baseline-grit`, which only applies to headline rows); if that invocation failed (a baseline failure aborts the run) it was retried once without the baseline. v0.5.0 cannot run the blame, stash, log (--limit/--json), pull/rebase and push/force-with-lease headline commands (and branch/merged), so those rows have baseline=null with baseline_note (not substituted). Per-scenario cap 600 s (300 s for the known-problem http/repack/pull-check/branch-rename/push-refspec ids, first pass). `runs` is the number of timed runs per tool (3 to 20 after warmup, policy default); stddev_ms is null everywhere because the daily runner reports medians only; max_rss_kb is the peak RSS of the timed process tree. Fixtures: git.git at v2.47.0, small, synth-10k and synth-100k pre-generated with `grit-bench fixtures prepare`; many-refs, many-refs-loose, big-blobs, deep-tree, deep-history and large-file fixtures built on demand by their scenarios. The repos block is copied from 2026-10-22 (same generators; `grit-bench fixtures list` counts re-checked: git-git 4525 files / 954 refs, small 100/60, synth-10k 10000/800, synth-100k 100000/1200).
Scenario set: every executable id found in grit-bench's daily registry (127 ids, excluding the test/* and future/* harness self-test ids). New since 2026-10-22: add/hunks@large-file, add/lines@large-file, branch/list-json@many-refs, branch/merged@many-refs, branch/merged-ref@many-refs, clone/shallow@git-git, log/limit-path@git-git, rebase/onto@git-git, rebase/onto@synth-10k, remote/remove@many-refs, remote/show@many-refs, restore/hunks@large-file, revs/count-path@git-git, tag/contains@git-git, tag/list-sort-version@git-git. Besides the 17 required headline scenarios, log/json-100, pull/rebase, push/force-with-lease, branch/list-json and branch/merged carry headline=true (grit-bench marks them headline).
Noise re-runs: compared with daily/latest.json of 2026-10-22 (grit/git time ratio more than 20% worse, or peak-RSS ratio more than 30% worse), 8 scenarios were re-run 3 more times (4 samples per tool; reported median_ms and max_rss_kb are the median of the four per-sample medians/peaks; per-row `rerun` records the sample count and the first-pass grit/git ratio; re-runs did not repeat the baseline): add/dry-run@synth-10k (mem), branch/create@many-refs, branch/list@many-refs (headline), hooks/list@small, init/empty@small, log/oneline-100@synth-100k, pick/one@synth-100k, status/dirty@small. Outcome: branch/list@many-refs (1.97x -> 1.50x, same as yesterday), init/empty@small (1.76x -> 1.52x), log/oneline-100@synth-100k (1.96x -> 1.58x) and status/dirty@small (2.44x -> 1.96x, same as yesterday) were noise; branch/create@many-refs (1.96x vs 1.50x yesterday), hooks/list@small (1.48x vs 1.13x), pick/one@synth-100k (1.22x vs 0.95x) and add/dry-run@synth-10k memory (1.87x vs 1.53x) reproduced. The first pass of the tag/contains and repack/full timeouts was also retried without the baseline binary (see below). New scenarios with no previous row were not re-run.
Failures (kept in the report with grit=null and an error; neither tool has a number): add/hunks@large-file and revs/count-path@git-git (the git side of the timed run exits 128), add/lines@large-file (prepare exits 1), clone/shallow@git-git (harness correctness check cannot spawn `rev-list --count`), push/refspec@git-git (grit push rejected as non-fast-forward in the harness correctness check), tag/contains@git-git (grit tag --contains spins at 100% CPU: a direct spot check on git.git ran 60 s without finishing versus ~0.7 s for `git tag -l --contains`), repack/full@git-git (did not finish in 600 s; same as yesterday). The http scenarios first failed because grit-http-server had not been built; it was built from the same main commit and clone/http, fetch/incremental-http and push/incremental-http were re-run with --http-server (all three completed this time; push/incremental-http@git-git is 3.1x slower than git and grit peaks at about 2 GB RSS, 6.4x git, there). Fixed since yesterday: pull/check@git-git now completes (grit 692 ms vs git 106 ms; it took minutes yesterday) and branch/rename@many-refs now runs (3.4x git). Caution: push/incremental@git-git has git at ~1.6 s versus grit at ~8 ms (and fetch/pull incremental similarly show grit far ahead of git and of v0.5.0, which takes 40 to 80 s); I did not independently verify these rows beyond the harness's own correctness checks.
